package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2022-22965, 'SpringShell') that allows attackers to write arbitrary files (such as JSP webshells) to the server via crafted POST parameters, leading to full server compromise.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (HTTP POST request with crafted parameters)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /path HTTP/1.1
Host: vulnerable-server
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

malicious_snippets.code_language: java (parameter binding exploit via HTTP POST)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code binds HTTP POST parameters to internal Java class properties, allowing an attacker to write a malicious JSP file to the webroot, resulting in remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The ability to bind arbitrary POST parameters to internal Java class properties is highly abnormal and allows attackers to manipulate the application’s class loader and file system.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal data binding should only affect user-defined model objects, not internal class loader or file system properties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate data binding is used for mapping form fields to POJOs, but never to internal Java classes.
key_indicators: Ability to write arbitrary files via HTTP parameters

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a crafted HTTP POST request with parameters targeting internal class loader properties.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JSP file is written to the webroot.

attack_chain.action: Attacker accesses the malicious JSP file via the web server, triggering remote code execution.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected file creation in webroot (e.g., shell.jsp)
JSP file uploads via parameter binding
file_indicators: Unexpected JSP files in Tomcat webroot
network_indicators: Unusual POST requests with class.module.classLoader.* parameters
Subsequent access to newly created JSP files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor HTTP POST requests for parameters matching class.module.classLoader.*. Alert on creation of new JSP files in the webroot directory. Correlate suspicious POST requests with subsequent access to those files. Use SCA tools to flag vulnerable Spring versions.
